compliant.txt.evidence: Items A and B passed with exact IDs and content tokens. Repair changed C. D depends on C and its dependency is declared, so C and D plus earlier findings are in the next request. A and B carry forward by exact mechanical comparison. An ID mismatch in E marks E changed, so E also reaches the next review request. The complete evaluator configuration (reviewer prompt, rubric, model/version, sampling settings and frozen reference) matches the earlier verdicts mechanically by exact values or hashes. A later rubric change counts every affected item as changed, so all affected items reach re-review before aggregate acceptance.

violating.txt.evidence: The repair reviewer receives the whole unit again, including unchanged passing items A and B.

near-miss.txt.evidence: The reviewer says A looks unchanged, so A carries forward without an exact identity comparison. reviewer judgment used as item identity. Separately, B carries forward by matching ID and content even though its reviewer rubric changed: carried verdict from a different evaluator configuration.
near-miss.txt.non_substitute: reviewer judgment used as item identity
